name: JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd. (晶科能源) — incl. Jinko Solar Co. (SSE STAR: 688223) and Jinko ESS
employees: not disclosed on fetched first-party pages (see 20-F)
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Jinko is the world's #1 PV module shipper (tied with LONGi in 2025) taking its first annual loss in 12 years to the solar price war — and management has explicitly designated energy storage (SunTera BESS, 5.2 GWh shipped in 2025, guided to more than double in 2026) as the 'second growth engine' to restore profitability, with a new AI-data-center solar+storage play ('Sunny 365' AIDC, plus a planned 1 GW Ningxia data center) opening a third front. BACKGROUND: JinkoSolar Holding (NYSE: JKS) holds ~54% of Jiangxi Jinko (SSE STAR: 688223). Flagship Tiger Neo N-type TOPCon modules (>400 GW cumulative delivered — a world first); >10 manufacturing bases across China, the US (Jacksonville, FL), Southeast Asia, and the Middle East; sales in ~200 countries. FY2025: revenue RMB 65.5B (−29%), net loss RMB 4.45B; Q1 2026 gross margin recovered to 8.3%.
ecosystemRole: We assess Jinko as a PV giant becoming a storage challenger: BNEF Tier-1 ESS maker for 8 straight quarters and 12 GWh of claimed ESS capacity, but absent from top-10 BESS integrator rankings (Wood Mackenzie/EnergyTrend) — a fast-growing niche player against Sungrow/BYD/CATL/Tesla scale. Its differentiation is the integrated solar-plus-storage sell (SunTera grid-forming BESS + Tiger Neo modules) now packaged for AI data centers with claimed 800V HVDC architecture compatibility — the first module maker to also move into data-center operation itself (planned 1 GW Ningxia campus).

productsAndServices.name: PV Modules — Tiger Neo (N-type TOPCon)
productsAndServices.description: Flagship Tiger Neo platform: cumulative shipments ~240 GW by Q1 2026; Tiger Neo 3.0 (launched Sept 2025) delivers 670 W at 24.8% module efficiency (AIDC variant 680 W / 25.17%), 85±5% bifaciality, −0.26%/°C temperature coefficient, 30-year performance warranty. Capacity roadmap: end-2026 target of 120 GW wafer / 95 GW cell / 130 GW module, ~100 GW integrated including 14 GW overseas. US-market EAGLE modules assembled in Jacksonville, FL (650+ workers, since 2018).
highlights: #1 global module shipper: 92.9 GW in 2024; 86 GW in 2025 (7th straight year, tied #1 with LONGi per InfoLink)
731 N-type TOPCon patents claimed; RETC 'Overall Highest Achiever' 7 consecutive years; TÜV Rheinland shading/hail verification (June 2026)
Tiger Neo 3.0 global rollout explicitly excludes the US — a tariff-era product-segmentation decision
10 GW Saudi cell/module JV with PIF's RELC and Vision Industries (announced July 2024)
productsAndServices.positioning: Top of a brutally consolidating market: top-4 makers ≈58% of 536 GW ranked 2025 shipments, entire Chinese chain loss-making through 2024–25; US trade barriers include combined rates up to ~246% on its Vietnam output plus the unresolved 2023 Jacksonville raid backdrop
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct to developers/EPCs/IPPs and distribution; ~80%+ of Q1 2026 module shipments overseas
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Utility-scale, C&I, and distributed solar globally; AIDC-variant modules for data-center campuses
productsAndServices.roadmap: FY2026 module guidance 75–85 GW; 'anti-involution' policy-driven price recovery is the margin variable

productsAndServices.name: Energy Storage — SunTera / SunGiga (Jinko ESS)
productsAndServices.category: BESS · the designated second growth engine
productsAndServices.description: Utility-scale SunTera line: G2 (5.015 MWh, 314 Ah) and G3 (6.25 MWh, 587 Ah cells, >95% RTE, grid-forming modes incl. black start and microgrid operation — global shipments from Q4 2025); C&I SunGiga line (215–522 kWh liquid-cooled cabinets; G2 Plus adds AI price-forecasting EMS for energy trading); US-market EAGLE Storage variants (DCB-5000/6250, ACB-261) with cybersecurity provisions; 12 GWh of claimed ESS manufacturing capacity.
highlights: 5.2 GWh shipped in 2025 (only ~1.7 GWh revenue-recognized); Q1 2026: 1.42 GWh shipped; signed + high-probability orders >10 GWh
2026 guidance: more than double 2025 shipments; management guides storage growing 100–150% annually over the next three years
Chairman Li Xiande: storage is 'a primary driver for enhancing our profitability profile' — the explicit loss-offset strategy
China only 10–15% of ESS sales — focus is Europe, LatAm, Middle East, APAC; US ~600 MWh in 2025 with a 2026 'breakthrough' targeted
productsAndServices.positioning: BNEF Tier-1 ESS provider 8 consecutive quarters but not yet in any top-10 integrator ranking — a credible fast-follower whose bundled solar+storage channel is the wedge, not standalone BESS scale
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct supply agreements with developers/EPCs/IPPs (Sunrev 1 GWh framework; Marubeni in Japan) plus EU distribution
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Utility solar-plus-storage, standalone grid services, C&I energy trading, and (new) AI data centers
productsAndServices.roadmap: SunTera G3 global ramp through 2026; >10 GWh order conversion; US market entry expansion

productsAndServices.name: Sunny 365 — AI Data-Center Solar+Storage (2026)
productsAndServices.description: Integrated PV+ESS+EMS solution family launched August 2026; the AIDC edition pairs 680 W / 25.17% Tiger Neo 3.0 AIDC modules with SunTera storage for 24/7 green supply and resilient backup — claiming grid-forming support, seamless on/off-grid switching, and compatibility with 800V HVDC data-center power architecture. Alongside it: a company plan for a 1 GW AI data center near Zhongwei, Ningxia (~530,000 m²; groundbreaking 2026, completion ~2028) — the first module maker to move into data-center operation.
highlights: Positions Jinko on the demand side of its own products — 'from power supply to demand management'
A desert AI-data-center power-supply role is reported by Nikkei/KrAsia but not company-confirmed in accessible filings — treat as unverified
productsAndServices.positioning: Unique among module makers; overlaps conceptually with Google's Intersect-style energy-park model, executed from the supplier side
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Solution sales; the Ningxia campus may involve bank financing/JVs per reports
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Chinese AI data-center operators; retail/supermarket edition announced for distributed C&I

recentDevelopments.read: Chinese financial press reads the founding 'iron triangle' fracturing under loss pressure; company cites personal reasons — the governance shift bears watching through the turnaround.

recentDevelopments.headline: Tiger Neo 3.0 launched: 670 W, 24.8% module efficiency, 27% cell efficiency
recentDevelopments.read: Spec leadership maintained through the trough — but the global rollout excludes the US, conceding that market to tariff math.

recentDevelopments.headline: SunTera G3 unveiled: 6.25 MWh, 587 Ah cells, grid-forming (black start, microgrid); global shipments from Q4 2025
recentDevelopments.read: The storage flagship matches the 6+ MWh class of Sungrow/Hithium/BYD — grid-forming capability is the differentiator pitch for weak-grid markets.

recentDevelopments.headline: US Commerce final AD/CVD determinations: Jinko-specific combined rates up to ~246% on Vietnam-made modules
recentDevelopments.read: The US module door narrows to Jacksonville assembly; ROTH called the determinations 'negative for JinkoSolar' — storage and non-US markets carry the growth burden.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess storage is a survival strategy, not diversification: with module gross margin at 2.2% for FY2025 and the whole Chinese chain loss-making, the ESS ramp (5.2 GWh → >10 GWh guided) is management's stated primary profitability lever. Basis: earnings calls and the chairman's own framing.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the analyst view is that storage is a margin story, not yet a revenue replacement: 2026 consensus EPS was revised up sharply on margin recovery while revenue forecasts stayed flat (~RMB 92B) — the recovery depends on 'anti-involution' price discipline holding as much as on Jinko's own execution.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the AIDC moves (Sunny 365, the Ningxia 1 GW campus) are a demand-side hedge: owning/serving data-center load monetizes Jinko's own solar+storage output in-country while US trade barriers cap its western module business — an unproven but structurally logical pivot.

(Moderate confidence) We assess governance transition is a live risk: the founding family controlled ~55.6% of the holdco, and co-founder Kangping Chen's full 2026 exit amid the first loss in 12 years leaves professional managers (ex-CFO Cao) running the operating company through its hardest stretch.

(Low confidence) The reported desert AI data-center power-supply arrangement (Nikkei/KrAsia) and the polysilicon consolidation fund are both unconfirmed — either would materially change the economics if realized.
